result.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
result.summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. Actor adaptation estimates on-policy memory value within rollout groups with and without memory, using a reward that prioritizes resolution and penalizes step count in successful runs. Provenance-gated value credit assigns the additional value term to steps identified as using memory-supplied anchors, while every step retains outcome credit. On ChainSWE, CoReMem raises the 27B actor's resolve rate from 21.0% to 25.7%, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens, including memory-module calls, relative to the untrained actor model without memory.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoReMem，把记忆的读写成本纳入设计：用下一任务上有无某段轨迹的反事实对比来估值仓库记忆锚点（位置与可执行检查），并以带步数惩罚的 on-policy 奖励和溯源门控信用分配适配 actor。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有/无某段轨迹」的分段估值与溯源门控信用分配，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容的贡献分配与 THINK/STOP 成本收益建模，但对象是代码仓库的显式文本记忆而非视觉内部状态，迁移线索需较多核查。
